topics.label: Introduction to Cancer Hallmarks and Lecture Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session's learning objectives, reviews tumor progression models, and establishes the Hanahan and Weinberg hallmarks of cancer framework.

topics.label: Sustained Proliferation and Growth Signaling Pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how oncogenic mutations in cell surface receptor pathways and intracellular cascades drive autonomous proliferation and evade growth inhibition.

topics.label: Block to Differentiation in Hematopoietic and Epithelial Cancers
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how cancer cells evade terminal lineage specification in both hematopoietic lineages and the intestinal crypt epithelium.

topics.label: Resistance to Apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how mutations disrupting the balance of pro-apoptotic and anti-apoptotic factors prevent programmed cell death in cancer cells.

topics.label: Telomere Maintenance, Senescence, and Stress Signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how telomere maintenance overcomes cellular senescence limits and how stress signaling activates tumor-suppressive p53 checkpoints.

topics.label: Altered Cancer Metabolism and Oncometabolites
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how tumors reprogram cellular metabolism toward aerobic glycolysis and how metabolic enzyme mutations produce epigenetic-modifying oncometabolites.

topics.label: Tumor Angiogenesis and the Angiogenic Switch
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the requirement, timing, and regulatory balance of blood vessel recruitment to sustain tumor growth.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Progression of Cancer Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the biological steps, clinical detection, and clonal characteristics of tumor dissemination to distant organs.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Final Remarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by summarizing the integration of cancer hallmarks and referencing recent updates to the conceptual framework.
